title: Loom Review 2026: Is Async Video the Ultimate Replacement for Meetings?
content:
*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

## Quick Answer

**Loom** is the leading asynchronous video messaging platform, now part of the Atlassian ecosystem after its $975 million acquisition in 2023. With over **25 million users** across 400,000+ companies including Netflix, HubSpot, and Shopify, Loom has become the de facto standard for replacing unnecessary meetings with quick, shareable video recordings. Starting with a generous **free plan** (up to 25 videos per person) and scaling to Business at **$15/user/mo** (billed annually) with AI-powered features like auto-summaries, filler word removal, and meeting recaps, Loom delivers exceptional value for remote and hybrid teams. If you spend more than 2 hours per week in status update meetings, Loom will pay for itself in the first month. It is, without question, the best async video tool on the market in 2026.

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **Incredibly easy to use** — One-click recording from desktop, browser extension, or mobile. No learning curve whatsoever. Record screen, cam, or both simultaneously.
- **Instant sharing via link** — No uploading, no downloading, no file size limits. Copy the link and paste it anywhere — Slack, email, Notion, Jira — and it just works.
- **Generous free plan** — Up to 50 workspace members, 25 videos per person (5 minutes each), viewer analytics, and basic editing. More than enough for individual creators and small teams testing the waters.
- **Powerful AI suite (Business + AI)** — Auto-titles, auto-summaries, auto-chapters, filler word removal, silence removal, and the new AI meeting notes/recaps. The AI features genuinely save time, not just gimmicks.
- **Atlassian ecosystem integration** — Deep native integrations with Jira, Confluence, and Trello. If your team already uses Atlassian tools, Loom is a no-brainer.
- **Viewer engagement analytics** — Know exactly who watched your video, for how long, and whether they watched till the end. Includes emoji reactions and threaded comments.
- **Custom branding (Business plan)** — Add your company logo, custom colors, and branded sharing pages. Professional presentation out of the box.
- **Cross-platform** — Desktop apps for Mac and Windows, Chrome extension, iOS and Android apps. Record and watch from anywhere.

### Cons 👎

- **Free plan recording limit** — 5-minute cap per video on the free tier is restrictive for demos, tutorials, or detailed walkthroughs. Competitors like Vidyard offer longer free recordings.
- **AI features locked behind highest plan** — Auto-summaries, filler word removal, and meeting recaps require the $20/user/mo Business + AI plan. Competitors like Fireflies.ai include AI transcription for free.
- **No permanent free AI tier** — Unlike some competitors, Loom AI features are a limited trial on lower plans and require the full Business + AI subscription to retain.
- **Limited video editing capabilities** — You can trim the beginning and end, but there's no multi-track editing, transitions, or advanced effects. Loom is for quick async communication, not polished production.
- **No built-in transcription in lower plans** — Video transcripts (beyond AI-generated summaries) require the Business + AI plan or a third-party integration.
- **Enterprise pricing opacity** — No public pricing for Enterprise; requires contacting sales. Can be a friction point for procurement teams.

---

## Pricing Overview

Loom offers four tiers designed to scale from individual creators to global enterprises. All prices are per user, per month:

| Plan | Monthly Price | Annual Price (per mo) | Key Features |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Starter (Free)** | $0 | $0 | 25 videos/person (5 min max), screen + cam recording, instant sharing, viewer analytics, basic editing |
| **Business** | $18 | $15 | Unlimited videos & length, custom branding, engagement insights, embed links, password-protected videos |
| **Business + AI** ⭐ | $24 | $20 | All Business features + Loom AI: auto-titles, summaries, chapters, filler word removal, silence removal, auto CTAs, meeting notes & recaps, AI workflows, variables |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom | Everything in Business + AI + SSO, SCIM, advanced admin controls, dedicated support, custom data retention policies, zero data retention for AI |

⭐ **Our recommendation:** The **Business + AI plan at $20/user/mo** (annual) is the sweet spot. The AI features — particularly auto-summaries and filler word removal — deliver immediate ROI by saving 3-5 minutes of editing per video. For a team of 10 recording 5 videos each per week, that's 150-250 minutes saved weekly.

### Free Plan Deep Dive

The Starter plan is genuinely usable, not a crippled trial:
- ✅ Screen + cam recording with drawing tools
- ✅ Instant link sharing (never expires)
- ✅ Viewer analytics (who watched, how long)
- ✅ Comments and emoji reactions
- ✅ Up to 50 workspace members
- ✅ Chrome extension + desktop + mobile apps
- ❌ 5-minute recording limit per video
- ❌ 25 video limit per person (total, not per month)
- ❌ No custom branding
- ❌ AI features limited trial only

The 25-video total cap (not monthly) is the real limitation — once you hit 25 videos, you must delete old ones to record new content. This nudges active users toward the Business plan.

---

## Core Features Deep Dive

### Recording Experience

Loom's recording interface is its crown jewel. Click the record button, choose your capture mode (screen only, cam only, or both), and start talking. You can pause and resume mid-recording, draw on the screen with annotation tools, and toggle your camera on/off without stopping. The experience is identical across desktop app, Chrome extension, and mobile — a rare feat of UX consistency.

**Recording modes:**
- **Screen + Cam:** Picture-in-picture bubble overlay. Most popular for walkthroughs and presentations.
- **Screen Only:** Full-screen capture for demos, tutorials, and code reviews.
- **Cam Only:** Talking-head style for quick updates and personal messages.
- **Meeting Recording (NEW):** Auto-record and transcribe meetings via integration with Google Meet and Zoom.

### AI Features (Business + AI Plan)

Loom's AI suite, launched in 2024 and significantly expanded in 2025-2026, is the product's most compelling differentiator:

| AI Feature | What It Does | Time Saved |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto-Titles** | Generates a descriptive title based on video content | 10-15 seconds |
| **Auto-Summaries** | Creates a TL;DR paragraph + bullet points | 2-3 minutes |
| **Auto-Chapters** | Segments long videos into timestamped chapters | 1-2 minutes |
| **Filler Word Removal** | Removes "um," "uh," "like," "you know" with one click | 5-10 minutes of re-recording |
| **Silence Removal** | Trims dead air and pauses automatically | 3-5 minutes of manual trimming |
| **Auto CTA** | Adds a clickable call-to-action button at the end of your video | 30 seconds |
| **Meeting Notes & Recaps (NEW)** | Auto-generates structured meeting notes with action items, decisions, and timestamps | 15-20 minutes per meeting |
| **AI Workflows** | Chain AI actions — e.g., record → auto-summarize → create Jira ticket → post summary to Slack | 5-10 minutes per workflow |
| **Variables** | Personalize video titles, CTAs, and descriptions at scale using merge fields (e.g., "Hey {{first_name}}, here's your onboarding walkthrough") | Hours for scaled communication |

**The filler word removal alone is worth the upgrade.** Most people don't realize how many "ums" they say until they watch themselves. One click cleans up your entire video without re-recording — it's genuinely magical.

### Sharing and Collaboration

Loom's sharing model eliminates friction:
1. **Copy link** — Instant, no processing time for short videos
2. **Paste anywhere** — Slack unfurls a preview with thumbnail; email clients show an animated GIF preview; Notion and Jira embed the player inline
3. **Viewers watch without an account** — No sign-up required. They see your video immediately.

**Collaboration features:**
- **Comments:** Threaded, timestamp-linked comments on specific video moments
- **Emoji reactions:** Quick feedback at any point in the video (👏, 🎉, 💡, etc.)
- **@mentions:** Tag teammates in comments to draw their attention to specific timestamps
- **Password protection:** Restrict access to sensitive videos (Business+)
- **Viewer download control:** Toggle whether viewers can download the video file

### Viewer Analytics

Loom provides surprisingly detailed viewer analytics:
- **Who watched:** Individual viewer identification (requires Loom account) or anonymous viewer count
- **Watch percentage:** See exactly where viewers dropped off
- **View duration:** Total time spent watching
- **CTA clicks:** How many clicked your call-to-action button
- **Email notifications:** Get notified when specific people watch your video

For sales teams, the analytics are gold: you know exactly which prospects watched your demo and for how long, enabling perfectly timed follow-ups.

### Integrations

Loom's integration ecosystem — supercharged by the Atlassian acquisition — includes:

**Deep native integrations:**
- **Jira:** Embed Loom videos directly in issues; auto-create bugs from video feedback
- **Confluence:** Embed videos in documentation pages with one paste
- **Trello:** Attach video walkthroughs to cards
- **Slack:** Unfurl video previews with thumbnails; record and share without leaving Slack
- **Notion:** Paste a Loom link and it embeds an interactive player
- **Linear:** Attach videos to issues for bug reports and feature requests

**Zapier & Make integrations** enable hundreds of automated workflows:
- New Loom video → Create Asana task
- New Loom video → Send Slack message to #general channel
- New Loom video → Save to Google Drive
- New Loom video → Create HubSpot contact note

---

## Use Cases: Who Is Loom For?

### 1. Remote & Hybrid Teams ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Loom replaces status update meetings, daily standups, and "quick sync" calls. A 3-minute Loom saying "here's what I did yesterday and what I'm doing today" replaces a 30-minute meeting for 8 people. The math is undeniable: 3 minutes of recording saves 240 person-minutes.

**Best features for remote teams:** Async standups, meeting recaps with action items, viewer analytics to confirm everyone watched.

### 2. Engineering & Product Teams ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Engineers use Loom for code walkthroughs, bug reports, and PR explanations. Instead of writing a 500-word PR description, record a 2-minute screen share walking through the changes. Reviewers understand context faster and approve PRs sooner.

**Best features for engineering:** Screen recording with drawing tools, Jira/Linear integration, timestamp-linked comments, auto-chapters for long technical walkthroughs.

### 3. Sales & Customer Success ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Sales teams use Loom for personalized outreach, proposal walkthroughs, and demo follow-ups. A personalized video saying "Hey {{first_name}}, I recorded a quick walkthrough of the features we discussed" has significantly higher response rates than text emails.

**Best features for sales:** Variables (personalize at scale), viewer analytics (see who watched), CTAs (book a meeting, view pricing), custom branding.

### 4. Customer Support ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Support teams use Loom to show — not tell — solutions. A screen recording demonstrating exactly how to fix an issue resolves tickets faster than 5 back-and-forth emails with screenshots.

**Best features for support:** Quick recording, instant link sharing, viewer verification (no account needed), embed in help docs.

### 5. Education & Training ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Creating onboarding videos, training materials, and course content is effortless with Loom. Record once, share the link with unlimited viewers, and update anytime.

**Best features for training:** Auto-chapters for navigation, auto-summaries for TL;DR, embed anywhere, unlimited viewers.

### 6. Design & Creative Teams ⭐⭐⭐

Designers use Loom to present mockups, walk through Figma prototypes, and explain design decisions asynchronously. Faster than scheduling a 30-minute design review.

**Best features for design:** Screen + cam recording, annotation tools, comment threads for async feedback.

---

## Loom vs Competitors

| Feature | **Loom** | Vidyard | Snagit | ScreenPal (Screencast-O-Matic) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Free plan** | 25 videos (5 min) | Unlimited (limited features) | 15-day trial only | 15-min recordings |
| **AI features** | ✅ Auto-summaries, chapters, filler removal, meeting notes | ✅ AI script generation, coaching | ❌ No AI | ❌ Basic only |
| **Starting price (paid)** | $15/user/mo | $19/user/mo | $62.99 (one-time) | $4/user/mo |
| **Best for** | Async communication, remote teams | Sales outreach, prospecting | Detailed screenshots + annotations | Budget screen recording |
| **Unique strength** | Instant sharing, AI suite, Atlassian ecosystem | Sales-focused analytics and CRM integration | Best screenshot + annotation tool | Lowest price point |
| **Video editing** | Trim only | Basic trimming | Full editing suite | Basic editor included |
| **G2 Rating** | ⭐ 4.7/5 (2,000+) | ⭐ 4.5/5 (1,700+) | ⭐ 4.6/5 (1,000+) | ⭐ 4.4/5 (700+) |

**Verdict:** Loom wins for async team communication and general-purpose video messaging. Vidyard is better for dedicated sales teams needing CRM integration. Snagit is the choice for detailed technical documentation with annotated screenshots. ScreenPal is the budget option for basic screen recording.

---

## The Atlassian Effect: What the Acquisition Changed

Atlassian acquired Loom in October 2023 for $975 million — one of the largest acquisitions in the productivity space. Since then:

**What improved:**
- **Jira & Confluence integration** reached native-app quality — Loom videos embed and play inline with full functionality
- **Enterprise features** accelerated: SSO, SCIM, advanced admin controls, and compliance certifications were fast-tracked
- **AI investment** increased significantly: Loom AI features were launched and iterated faster than an independent startup could manage
- **Stability & infrastructure** benefited from Atlassian's global cloud infrastructure

**What hasn't changed:**
- Loom remains a standalone product — no Atlassian account required
- The free plan is still generous and independent of any Atlassian subscription
- The product roadmap continues to focus on async video, not being a bolt-on to Jira

**What to watch:** Atlassian's track record with acquisitions (Trello, Opsgenie, Halp) is mixed — some products thrive, others stagnate. So far, Loom has thrived, but long-term independence within a large organization is always uncertain.

---

## Real-World ROI: How Much Time Does Loom Save?

Let's run the numbers for a typical 10-person remote team:

| Scenario | Before Loom | After Loom | Time Saved (per week) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily standup (15 min × 10 people) | 750 person-minutes | 30 min recording + 50 min watching = 80 person-minutes | **670 min** |
| Weekly project status meeting (45 min × 10) | 450 person-minutes | 5 min recording + 30 min watching = 35 person-minutes | **415 min** |
| Design review (30 min × 5 people) | 150 person-minutes | 5 min recording + 15 min watching = 20 person-minutes | **130 min** |
| Bug report write-up (15 min per bug, 5 bugs) | 75 person-minutes | 3 min recording × 5 = 15 person-minutes | **60 min** |
| **Total weekly savings** | — | — | **1,275 person-minutes (21+ hours)** |

At a fully-loaded cost of $50/hour per employee, that's **$1,062 saved per week** — or over **$55,000 per year** for a 10-person team. Loom's Business + AI plan costs $2,400/year for that team. **ROI: 2,200%.**

Even if you only replace half of those meetings, the ROI is still 1,100%. The math is compelling.

---

## Getting Started with Loom

### Quick Setup (under 2 minutes)
1. **Sign up** at loom.com — free, no credit card required
2. **Install** the desktop app (Mac/Windows) or Chrome extension
3. **Record** your first video by clicking the Loom icon and selecting your capture mode
4. **Share** the automatically-copied link via Slack, email, or any platform

### Pro Tips for Better Looms
- **Keep it short:** 2-5 minutes is the sweet spot. If you need more than 10 minutes, it should probably be a live meeting.
- **Use the drawing tools:** Circle important elements, draw arrows, and highlight key areas. Visual emphasis keeps viewers engaged.
- **Start with a hook:** "Hey team, here's the quick update on Project X — the key takeaway is..." Don't bury the lead.
- **End with a clear CTA:** "Please review and leave comments by Thursday" or "Click the button below to book a follow-up call."
- **Enable AI summaries:** It takes 2 seconds and makes your video scannable for viewers who can't watch right now.

---

## Final Verdict

**Loom is the best async video communication tool on the market in 2026. Period.**

It's not the cheapest (ScreenPal starts at $4/mo). It's not the most feature-rich for video editing (Snagit has a full editor). And it's not the best for pure sales outreach (Vidyard edges it out on CRM integration). But for the core use case — replacing meetings with quick, shareable, AI-enhanced video messages — nothing comes close.

The Atlassian acquisition has accelerated development without compromising the product's independence. The AI features are genuinely useful, not gimmicky. The free plan is generous enough to prove value before paying. And the ROI math is undeniable: if your team spends more than 2 hours per week in status update meetings, Loom pays for itself in the first month.

**Our recommendation: Start with the free plan. If you hit the 25-video limit or need AI features, upgrade to Business + AI at $20/user/mo (annual). The filler word removal and auto-summaries alone justify the upgrade.**

**Rating: 94/100 — Highly Recommended.** ✅

mainEntity.name: Is Loom really free? What are the limitations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Loom offers a genuinely usable free Starter plan. It includes screen and camera recording, instant link sharing, viewer analytics, and up to 50 workspace members. Limitations: each person gets 25 total videos (not per month) capped at 5 minutes each. Once you hit 25 videos, you must delete older ones to record new content. The free plan does not include AI features (limited trial only), custom branding, or password-protected videos.

mainEntity.name: How much does Loom cost for teams?

acceptedAnswer.text: Loom Business costs $15/user/month billed annually ($18/month billed monthly). This includes unlimited videos, unlimited recording length, custom branding, engagement insights, embed links, and password protection. The Business + AI plan costs $20/user/month billed annually ($24/month monthly) and adds all AI features: auto-titles, auto-summaries, auto-chapters, filler word removal, silence removal, auto CTAs, meeting notes/recaps, AI workflows, and video variables. Enterprise pricing is custom and requires contacting sales.

mainEntity.name: What AI features does Loom offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Loom AI (available on the Business + AI plan) includes: Auto-Titles (generates descriptive video titles automatically), Auto-Summaries (creates TL;DR paragraphs with bullet points), Auto-Chapters (segments videos into timestamped chapters), Filler Word Removal (removes 'um,' 'uh,' 'like' with one click), Silence Removal (trims dead air and pauses), Auto CTA (adds clickable call-to-action buttons), Meeting Notes & Recaps (NEW — auto-generates structured meeting notes with action items and decisions), AI Workflows (chain multiple AI actions together), and Variables (personalize video titles and CTAs at scale using merge fields).

mainEntity.name: How does Loom compare to Vidyard?

acceptedAnswer.text: Loom excels at general async team communication with its superior ease of use, instant sharing, and AI features. Vidyard is better for dedicated sales teams that need CRM integration, detailed prospect analytics, and video email tracking. Loom starts at $15/user/mo (Business) vs Vidyard's $19/user/mo. Loom's free plan is more generous for basic use (25 videos vs limited features). For most teams replacing internal meetings, Loom is the better choice. For sales teams doing cold outreach at scale, Vidyard edges ahead.

mainEntity.name: Does Loom work with Atlassian tools (Jira, Confluence, Trello)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and the integration is excellent since Atlassian acquired Loom in 2023 for $975 million. You can embed Loom videos directly in Jira issues and Confluence pages — they play inline with full functionality. Loom videos can be attached to Trello cards as well. The integration is native-quality: paste a Loom link into any Atlassian product and it automatically unfurls an interactive video player. No plugins or configuration needed.

mainEntity.name: Do viewers need a Loom account to watch my videos?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Anyone with the link can watch your Loom video without creating an account or signing in. The video plays directly in their browser. Viewers only need an account if they want to leave comments, add emoji reactions, or access password-protected videos (depending on your sharing settings). This frictionless viewing experience is one of Loom's biggest advantages over tools that require recipients to create accounts or download files.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Loom on mobile devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Loom has dedicated iOS and Android apps that support screen recording, camera recording, and instant sharing. The mobile apps are full-featured and sync seamlessly with the desktop and web versions. You can record, view, comment on, and share videos from your phone or tablet. The mobile recording quality matches desktop in terms of resolution and frame rate, though annotation tools are more limited on smaller screens.

mainEntity.name: What video editing features does Loom include?

acceptedAnswer.text: Loom's editing capabilities are intentionally minimal because it's designed for quick, casual communication — not polished video production. You can trim the beginning and end of videos, and AI features handle filler word removal and silence trimming automatically (Business + AI plan). There is no multi-track editor, transitions, text overlays, or advanced effects. If you need professional-grade editing, record with Loom and then import the downloaded video file into a proper editor like Descript, Camtasia, or DaVinci Resolve. For most async communication use cases, Loom's editing is sufficient.

mainEntity.name: Is Loom secure for business use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Loom offers enterprise-grade security features including: SOC 2 Type II compliance, SSO and SCIM provisioning (Enterprise plan), password-protected videos (Business plan), viewer access controls (restrict to specific email domains), custom data retention policies, and zero data retention for AI features on Enterprise plans. Videos are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256). Loom's infrastructure runs on AWS and benefits from Atlassian's enterprise security investments post-acquisition. For regulated industries, the Enterprise plan with custom data policies is recommended.

mainEntity.name: Can Loom replace my daily standup meetings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely — this is one of Loom's most popular use cases. Instead of a 15-minute synchronous standup meeting with 10 people (consuming 150 person-minutes), each team member records a 2-3 minute Loom video sharing their progress, blockers, and plans. Team members watch asynchronously at their convenience. For a 10-person team, this saves approximately 110-120 person-minutes per standup — over 9 hours per week. The viewer analytics feature lets you confirm everyone watched. For teams considering async standups, we recommend starting with 2 async days per week and gradually increasing as the team adapts.
